newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus proposes corporate tax breaks.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus proposes corporate tax breaks.

text.p: Cyprus's finance minister disclosed plans on Friday to reduce corporate taxes by five percentage points as an incentive for the listing of new companies on the country's fledging stock exchange.

"The government is proceeding...with the reduction of the corporate tax by five percentage points for new companies which...introduce titles to the exchange," Finance Minister Christodoulos Christodoulou told a news conference.

He said the government's legal services were now processing the suggestion along with other changes on the legal definition of public companies for income tax purposes. The proposals have to be ratified by parliament.
Corporate tax rates in Cyprus now stand at 20 percent on net income below 40,000 pounds ($79.5 million) and 25 percent above that figure.
Christodoulou said the proposed changes would add new impetus to efforts to develop the bourse, which opened under its official framework in March 1996 after years of unofficial operations.
It now trades in 91 securities from 41 companies, and had a market capitalisation of 1.123 billion pounds at the end of March, up 6.39 percent from February.
"The CSE has already achieved remarkable results and its prospects are favourable," the minister said.

The news conference coincided with the invitation to tender by Cyprus's Central Bank for the auction of 21 million pounds in five year government development bonds with a coupon of seven percent. The bonds are due to start trading on the exchange later this month.
Bourse chairman Dinos Papadopoulos said full computerisation and paperless trading on the CSE is expected in the first six months of 1998.
He said that one of the most noteworthy achievements of the CSE was the implementation of the "T+9" settlement period, under which transactions must be completed within nine working days of a deal.
"It cannot be compared to the previous system prevailing where weeks or even months were needed to settle a transaction," Papadopoulos said.
The bourse has developed close working relations with other markets in the region, and especially the Athens stock exchange, he said.
"Interest has been shown for the introduction of Greek companies on the Cyprus exchange and vice-versa." The CSE is planning a promotional roadshow in Greece on May 9. ($0.502 pounds)
